summary: Cassia County cabin on Trapper Peak, dated only to the 1930s and listed as gone with no staffing record. No source describes what remains on the summit.

facts.status_note: Cabin listed as gone; no source describes what remains.

access.note: Roads of mixed quality reach the base and a 0.4-mile climb reaches the summit from the parking spot, per a climbing guide updated November 2019.

visit.trail_note: Climbing guide: about 0.4 miles and 285 feet of climbing from the parking spot to the summit.

evidence.supports: cabin dated to the 1930s, cited to Kresek

evidence.quote: We don't yet have a documented staffing history for this lookout.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: three short lookout listings, all with the 1930s date and none with a build year, and no staffing names. The 1967 Sundance-Trapper Peak fires in search results are a Boundary County story (oral histories on the Boundary County Museum site); they are probably a different peak and were not used. A geocache listing from search, which was not read, places a cache at the cabin site on a peak it calls Trapper Flat Peak; not cited. The lookout's elevation is 7892 ft on Idaho Fire Lookouts, not stored in facts because the story does not need it.
